newsitem.title: USA: Cargill to use steam pasteurization at beef plants.
newsitem.headline: Cargill to use steam pasteurization at beef plants.

text.p: Cargill Inc said its meat packing subsidiary, Excel Corp, will complete installation by June 1 of bacteria-cleansing steam pasteurization systems at its seven beef plants.

"We have been using the system with great success in some of our U.S. plants since the process was introduced," said Jerry Leising, Excel vice president and co-inventor of the pasteurization process, in a release.

Steam pasteurization was developed in 1995 by Cargill and Frigosandia Equipment Group, an international food processing equipment company. The process greatly reduces the risk of E.coli 0157.H7, which can cause serious and potentially fatal diseases.
The process uses steam at 180 degrees Fahrenheit to kill bacteria. No chemicals are used and meat color remains unaffected
Excel has seven beef plants in the U.S. and Canada, and industry sources rank Excel third in U.S. beef processor.
